newsitem.title: CHINA: China stocks end mixed, B shares thinly traded.
newsitem.headline: China stocks end mixed, B shares thinly traded.

text.p: China's stock markets closed mixed on Wednesday with turnover in foreign currency B shares dampened by concerns over corporate profits, brokers said.
A shares for Chinese investors ended the day higher on market talk of a cut in reserve requirements for local banks but analysts played down prospects for any such move.

Shanghai's B share index finished down 0.564 point or 0.77 percent to 72.931, with foreign investors bailing out of Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor and other blue chips seen posting disappointing interim results, brokers said.
B share turnover was $4.330 million against $3.482 million on Tuesday.
"Overseas funds are not willing to buy (Shanghai B shares) with the short-term market direction uncertain," one broker said.
"Concerns about interim results triggered the cutting of some positions and that pushed the index down."
Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor topped the active list and slid $0.012 or 2.99 percent to $0.388.
Huaxin Cement was the biggest Shanghai B share loser, also on talk of poor interim results. It tumbled $0.014 or 9.72 percent to $0.130.

Hainan Airlines fell $0.014 or 2.8 percent to $0.486 as trading resumed in the afternoon following a morning suspension. The airline said it was seeking compensation of about $2.25 million from an aircraft maintenance company for damage to one of its planes during routine repairs.

Shanghai's A share index rose 28.398 points or 2.35 percent to 1,234.456 as 347.4 million shares worth 3.5 billion yuan ($420 million) changed hands. The SSE30 blue chip index rose 64.068 points or 1.76 percent to 3,711.199.
The Shenzhen B share index scratched out a meagre gain of 0.34 point or 0.26 percent to 130.04 on turnover of HK$39 million against Tuesday's HK$25 million.
The domestic A share index for the nation's southern bourse was up 10.57 points or 2.66 percent to 407.72 on turnover of 4.6 billion yuan against 4.1 billion yuan in the previous session.
"Trading is very inactive (in Shenzhen's B share market)," said Cheng Li, an analyst at China Guotai Securities, referring to the B share market. "The index is still looking for support."
Brokers said investors were also waiting for listed firms to release their 1997 interim results. They are supposed to report by the end of August.
The prolonged weakness of Bengang Steel also cast a shadow over the Shenzhen B share market, said an analyst at Sun Hung Kai Investment Services Ltd in Shenzhen.
Bengang, which listed 400 million B shares early this month, closed unchanged at HK$2.00, still far below its offer price of HK$2.38.
Beijing Orient was the most actively traded Shenzhen B share company on volume of 5.08 million shares, rising HK$0.17 to HK$4.01 on expectations of solid interim earnings, brokers said.
